editorial:
Imagine waking up in a city full of flashing lights and loud cars when you are used to the quiet woods of 1835. That is exactly what happens to Op and Ed, two donut-shaped creatures called flummels. These guys are total goofballs who accidentally trip through time and land right in the middle of modern Shanghai. The vibe is light, colorful, and very silly. You will spend most of the movie laughing at how confused they are by things like fast food and traffic. It is a sweet story about friendship and trying to fit in when you are literally the only ones of your kind left on Earth.

What really works here is the fast pacing and the bright animation that makes the city feel alive. While the plot is pretty simple, the chemistry between the two main characters keeps you interested. Some parts feel a bit predictable, but it is meant for families, so that is okay.
endingExplained: After a wild chase through the city, Op and Ed find a way to use the time travel technology to go back to their own era. They manage to warn their fellow flummels about the future, which prevents their species from ever going extinct in the first place. The movie wraps up with them safely home, having learned that being different is okay, while the timeline is officially fixed for the better.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cute animals and silly time travel adventures.
similarMovies: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs
